plan: This is a first-price sealed-bid auction with a second-price payment rule (Vickrey auction). In such an auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the optimal strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This maximizes my profit in the long run by ensuring I win when my value is higher than the second-highest bid, and I never pay more than my value.

In a Vickrey auction, the optimal strategy is to bid your true value. This is a dominant strategy, meaning it's the best strategy regardless of what other bidders do. Bidding higher risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing a profitable auction. Since this is the first round and there's no history, I'll stick to this fundamental principle.

I will use a conservative bidding strategy to maximize profit. Since I only have one round, I need to be careful. I will bid slightly above the expected second-highest bid, assuming other bidders will bid close to their values. Given my value of $13, I will bid a bit lower than my value to ensure a positive profit margin if I win, but high enough to be competitive.
